newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after last minute rally.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after last minute rally.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher after late buying boosted values, but the market was thinly traded and no fresh news lay behind the gains.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said there were no fundamental factors behind the late surge in LME and COMEX which was probably due to some fund buying in thin volume.
"You have a lot of bearish views toward the market short-term. The market is just continuing to consolidate," O'Neill said. "The rally will have minimal upside potential."
LME stocks fell 1,475 tonnes Tuesday, but trading on the London exchange was generally thin throughout a session when the market slipped briefly into contango.
December COMEX settled 1.30 cents firmer at 88.45 cents per pound, traded 88.25 to 86.10 cents. Spot September went out 1.50 cents higher at 88.80 cents.
Volume was modest at an estimated 7,000 lots.
COMEX copper stocks fell Tuesday by 184 short tons to 19,486 short tons. COMEX stocks have begun falling steadily, although in modest tonnages each day.
